summary: I wrote 17 SRD tests for GLOSS.sphere at the end of tests/srd/test_glossary.py. They use Sleep, the only Sphere spell the engine has: a 5-ft-radius Sphere that affects each creature of your choice in it. All 17 pass. The engine measures the Sphere with the grid metric (diagonals count 5 ft), counts a creature exactly at the radius as inside, includes the point of origin, applies Total Cover from the origin (R-10), and leaves out named creatures outside the radius. No xfails were needed. Stage B marked SPELLS-02 / test_spells02_sleep as under-asserting: it now checks that each of the four creatures was in the Sphere centred on A (one save or automatic-success entry each) and that nobody was logged as outside it. I added one cheat to the abuse catalogue. Three tests depend on readings not yet in the register, so I proposed two rulings: the distance metric with the edge counting as inside, and the caster being in a Sphere centred on themself. Ruff check and format pass.

interactions.note: Whether the diagonal and edge squares are in a 5-ft Sphere depends on the metric: grid distance vs Euclidean. The diagonal boundary test follows the proposed grid metric.

A Sphere has the opposite rule: the origin is in the area. Tested with a creature on the origin, a named centre creature and a caster on their own origin, plus the negative that a caster away from the origin isn't in the Sphere (it isn't an Emanation).

interactions.with: R-10 / GLOSS.area-of-effect (Total Cover blocks the straight lines)
interactions.note: A creature inside the radius with Total Cover from the point of origin isn't affected.
The caller's list can only narrow the Sphere; a named creature outside it isn't caught.
A higher slot doesn't change the radius.
MIALEE auto-succeeds; her presence in the area shows as the automatic-success log entry.

abuse.case: Naming creatures for an area spell that the area can't hold (far from the point of origin)
abuse.reason: Sleep takes a caller list; the Sphere must still filter it.

abuse.case: Stretching an area by upcasting a spell whose higher levels don't enlarge it
abuse.reason: Sleep cast with a level 2 slot keeps its 5-ft radius.

abuse.case: Naming yourself for an area to be in it (a Sphere placed elsewhere isn't an Emanation)
abuse.reason: The origin is the chosen point, not the caster.

abuse.case: Reading a Sphere's radius as its diameter (new catalogue entry)
abuse.reason: Covered by the 10-ft boundary tests along the axis, the diagonal and upward.

abuse.case: Leaving creatures that are in the area off the list to spare them
abuse.reason: Doesn't apply: the only Sphere spell in scope (Sleep) is 'of your choice', so leaving a creature off the list legitimately spares it.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.sphere ambiguity 1: 'specifies the distance it extends as the radius': Euclidean distance or the grid metric, and is a point exactly at the radius inside?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Measure a Sphere's radius with the grid distance used for range and movement (each square, diagonals included, counts 5 ft; elevation counts the same way), from the centre of the origin's space to the centre of the creature's space. A creature exactly at the radius is inside, so a 5-ft Sphere covers the 3×3 block of squares around its origin and nothing 10 ft away.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.sphere ambiguity 3: 'A Sphere's point of origin is included': is a creature whose space holds the origin (including the caster) in the area?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A: a creature whose space holds the point of origin is in the Sphere and is affected like any other creature in it, including a caster who places the Sphere on their own space. This is the opposite of P-25/P-27 for Cones and Cubes. A caster away from the origin isn't in the Sphere: it isn't an Emanation.
